title: Digital Breakup: Emerging Adults’ Experiences of Ghosting, Digital Grief, and Romantic Relationship Dissolution
abstract: This study explored emerging adults’ experiences of romantic relationship dissolution in the digital age. Participants were 19 university students in Türkiye (12 women, 7 men; ages 20–24); focus group and individual interview data were analyzed thematically. Five themes were identified: emotional deficits and the burden of the unsaid; factors facilitating digital breakups; experiences and interpretations of ghosting; digital traces and recovery; and perceived relational dynamics in digital contexts. Digital breakups were often experienced as emotionally incomplete, although some participants found digital distance protective. Ghosting was interpreted in terms of ambiguity and power, primarily through recipients’ and observers’ accounts. Persistent digital traces complicated recovery, while participants associated digital environments with accelerated tempo, perceived alternatives, and platform-specific meanings. Examining these experiences in Türkiye extends digitally mediated dissolution research to an underrepresented cultural context in which participants emphasized respect, explanation, and interpersonal accountability during relationship endings.
